claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Intermediate-temperature annealing promotes local chemical segregation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Intermediate-temperature annealing promotes nanoscale chemical ordering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The annealing-induced segregation or ordering is localized at subgrain boundaries.
Limited atomic diffusion during intermediate annealing generates the local segregation or ordering.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations or ordering at subgrain boundaries lower the nucleation barrier for secondary phases.
The annealing-induced nanoscale precursors dictate the transformation pathway during rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching after intermediate annealing permits non-equilibrium secondary phases to emerge from the high-temperature BCC state.
Annealed-then-quenched samples will have a higher secondary-phase fraction than samples quenched directly from the high-temperature BCC state.
The annealed-then-quenched samples will exhibit observable nanoscale segregation associated with phase boundaries.
The proposed mechanism operates only within an annealing temperature-and-time window that permits sufficient but limited diffusion.
At annealing temperatures that are too low, the required nanoscale segregation may not develop.
At annealing temperatures that are too high, the required nanoscale segregation may not develop and the transformation pathway may remain unaffected.
With insufficient annealing duration, the required nanoscale segregation may not develop and the transformation pathway may remain unaffected.
